task:
This dataset is a panel of eight single human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (WTC-11 line with endogenously mEGFP-tagged alpha-actinin-2, ACTN2), fixed 32 days after the start of differentiation and imaged on a spinning-disk confocal with a 63x/1.2 NA water objective. Each image is the maximum-intensity projection of the ACTN2-mEGFP channel through the cell, cropped around one target cell. All eight cells come from the same differentiation and the same imaging session.

Files, for X = A to H:
- cell_X_actn2.ome.tif: ACTN2-mEGFP maximum projection, axes YX, uint16. The physical pixel size is recorded in the OME-XML metadata.
- cell_X_mask.ome.tif: 2D mask on the same grid. Pixels equal to 1 belong to the target cell; neighboring cells that fall inside the crop are 0.

Sarcomere length is the z-line to z-line spacing along the myofibrils. Determine which of the eight target cells contain striated myofibrils, meaning myofibrils with z-lines from which a sarcomere length can be measured. Then report the median sarcomere length across those cells only, using one representative value per cell, in micrometers.

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"striated_cell_ids": [<sorted list of cell ids, e.g. "cell_A">], "n_striated": <int>, "median_sarcomere_length_um": <float (micrometers)>}
</EVAL_ANSWER>
notes:
1. WHAT ARE YOU TESTING?
Whether the agent knows that a sarcomere length exists only where there are sarcomeres. In hiPSC-cardiomyocytes, ACTN2 also sits in z-bodies: puncta on premyofibrils and stress-fiber-like fibers, and scattered puncta in cells that have not assembled myofibrils. These cells carry no registered z-disks and have no sarcomere length. Every periodicity tool still returns a number for them, and that number lands in the physiological range: aligned peak-to-peak profiles give 1.96 to 2.35 um, a band-limited 2D FFT gives the edge of its search band (2.6 to 3.0 um), and the authors' own published GLCM peak distance gives 1.32 to 1.68 um. An agent that runs a sarcomere pipeline on every cell, or that decides striation from the neighbors in the crop instead of the masked target, gets the wrong cell set, the wrong count, and usually the wrong median. An agent that looks for a real sarcomeric peak (or simply looks at the cells as a cardiomyocyte biologist would) separates them cleanly.

2. GROUND TRUTH
Striated cells: cell_B, cell_D, cell_E (n_striated = 3). Median sarcomere length = 1.73 um.

Striation call. Gerbin et al. 2021 had two experts score every cell for alpha-actinin-2 organization on a 1 to 5 scale. As the scale is summarized in work built on this dataset (SarcNet, arXiv 2405.17926): 1 = sparse, disorganized puncta; 2 = denser, more organized puncta; 3 = puncta mixed with fibers and z-discs; 4 = regular but not aligned z-discs; 5 = almost organized and aligned z-discs. The authors' pixel classifier assigns each pixel to diffuse/other, fibers, disorganized puncta, organized puncta, or organized z-disks. Rule: striated if both expert scores are >= 4 and the organized z-disk fraction is >= 0.5; not striated if both scores are <= 2 and the z-disk fraction is <= 0.05. Score-3 cells were left out of the panel so that no cell is borderline. Image check in ground_truth.py: the local prominence of the in-band radial spectral peak (power at f0 over the geometric mean of power at 0.75 f0 and 1.33 f0) is 8.3 to 13.1 in the three striated cells and 0.8 to 1.4 in the other five, so the author annotation and the image agree for every cell. The non-striated radial spectra fall monotonically through the sarcomere band with no peak at all.

Per-cell table (lengths in um; experts = the two annotators; class fractions from the authors' classifier; 1a = whole-cell 2D power spectrum radial peak in 1.2-3.0 um; 2 = structure-tensor-aligned z-line profiles; GLCM = authors' published peak distance):

| cell_B | 5/4 | 0.87 | 0.11 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 13.14 | 1.686 | 1.776 | 1.80 | striated | 1.731 |
| cell_C | 1/1 | 0.00 | 0.59 | 0.39 | 0.00 | 0.79 | 4.57 (band edge) | 2.14 | 1.32 | not striated | none |
| cell_D | 5/5 | 0.87 | 0.12 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 8.26 | 1.655 | 1.734 | 1.80 | striated | 1.695 |
| cell_E | 5/5 | 0.93 | 0.01 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 9.43 | 1.734 | 1.812 | 1.80 | striated | 1.773 |

Per-cell sarcomere length is the mean of method 1a and method 2, the Task B v1 methods unchanged: 1a is a 3 um Gaussian high-pass, soft-edged mask, 2048-point FFT, radial average and parabolic peak refinement; 2 is nine parallel 12 um profiles per window along the local structure-tensor axis, sub-pixel peaks, median of window medians. Harmonic check: power at 2 f0 is 0.06 to 0.08 of the fundamental in the striated cells, so the in-band peak is the fundamental. Method-only medians across the three striated cells: 1a 1.686, tiles 1.678, 2 1.776. The authors' GLCM peak distance for the same three cells is 1.80 (whole pixels of 0.12 um).

3. TRAPS (each measured on these images by ground_truth.py)
a) Measuring every cell. Running a sarcomere pipeline on all eight cells and calling them all striated: n = 8, median 2.04 (aligned profiles), 2.48 (tile FFT), 2.75 (whole-cell FFT band maximum), 2.41 (GT method without the striation call). The puncta and fiber cells return 1.96 to 2.35 um by aligned profiles, values a reader would accept as sarcomere lengths.
b) Trusting a published-style periodicity metric. The authors' GLCM peak distance returns 1.32 to 1.68 um for the five non-striated cells; the all-cell median is 1.56, n = 8.
c) Judging striation from the crop instead of the target. The crops include striated neighbors. Without the mask, the 2D FFT finds a sarcomere peak at 1.83 (cell_A) and 1.75 um (cell_H), so a band-range test calls five cells striated (median 1.72, which passes on length but fails on the set and count). Using every unmasked crop gives n = 8, median 1.79.
d) Band-limited spectral maximum taken as a period without checking that a peak exists. In the non-striated cells the maximum sits at the long-wavelength edge of whatever band is searched (2.6 to 3.0 um for 1.2 to 3.0 um; cell_C refines to 4.57 um past the edge).

4. CHECKED AND NOT DISCRIMINATING
- A masked 2D FFT with any sanity test on the peak (a range of 1.5 to 2.2 um, or a prominence threshold anywhere from 2 to 8) recovers exactly cell_B, cell_D and cell_E with median 1.69. The task does not require sophisticated signal processing; it requires the agent to ask whether each cell has sarcomeres before measuring them.
- Visual inspection of the masked images separates the groups without ambiguity.

6. TOLERANCE AND GRADER RATIONALE
striated_cell_ids must match exactly (Jaccard 1.0) and n_striated must equal 3: the panel was built with no borderline cells, so there is one right set. The median has +/-0.12 um (one pixel, about 7%), window [1.61, 1.85], as in Task B v1. It spans the per-cell GT range (1.695 to 1.773), all three single-method medians (1.678 to 1.776) and the authors' GLCM value for the striated cells (1.80, quantized to whole 0.12 um pixels). The nearest failing all-cell median is 1.56 (GLCM) below and 2.04 (aligned profiles) above. A median from the right set computed with any reasonable method passes; the set and count are what the task discriminates on.

7. DATA FILES
Sixteen OME-TIFFs, 5.9 MB in total: cell_A ... cell_H, each an _actn2 image (uint16, YX, zlib) and a _mask (uint8, 1 = target cell), PhysicalSizeX/Y 0.1195257 um. Each image is channel 1 ('488', the maximum projection of ACTN2-mEGFP) of the authors' 10-channel 2D field from s3://allencell/aics/integrated_transcriptomics_structural_organization_hipsc_cm/2d_segmented_fields/, cropped with an 8 um margin around the target cell, pixel values unchanged. The mask is the target label of channel 9 ('cell'); its pixel count times 0.12^2 reproduces the authors' cell area. All eight cells are day 32, plate 5500000014, session 20190816_M02_001, whose raw files carry SlideBook calibration 0.1195257 um/px (tag 65007 and TIFF resolution). Source FOVs, labels and crop windows are in provenance/panel_author_annotations.csv; provenance/build_snapshot.py rebuilds the snapshot. Source: Gerbin et al. 2021, Cell Systems 12:670-687, doi:10.1016/j.cels.2021.05.001. Allen Institute for Cell Science terms of use (noncommercial).
